root_cause.text: The mcp23s08 driver does not initialize the MCP_GPINTEN register to zero during probe, so if the chip retains interrupt-on-change settings from a previous boot, the interrupt handler may be invoked for pins that lack a registered nested handler, causing a null pointer dereference in the spinlock.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `mcp_write(mcp, MCP_GPINTEN, 0)` before setting up the irq chip. The CVE description explicitly states that the issue was latent until commit f9f4fda15e72 removed reg_defaults, causing the actual hardware register value (which may be non-zero) to be read, triggering the crash.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable all pin interrupts during probe to prevent spurious interrupts before handlers are set up.
intent_record.what: Added a call to mcp_write to write 0 to MCP_GPINTEN register to disable all pin interrupts before setting up gpio_irq_chip, with an error return on failure.
intent_record.how: This change prevents the interrupt handler from being invoked for any pins that have interrupts enabled but no handler registered yet, thereby avoiding spurious or nested interrupt calls.

grouping_result.intent: Disable all pin interrupts during probe to prevent spurious interrupts before handlers are set up.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by disabling all pin interrupts during probe, which is exactly what was missing.

candidates.rationale: This line enables the IRQ chip for the GPIO controller but does not first clear the MCP_GPINTEN register to zero, leaving previous interrupt-on-change settings active. If any pin had interrupts enabled from a previous boot, the interrupt handler may be invoked for those pins without a registered nested handler, leading to a null pointer dereference.
